newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan stocks leap on Greenspan, blue-chip revival.
newsitem.headline: Japan stocks leap on Greenspan, blue-chip revival.

text.p: Japanese stocks soared by more than three percent on Friday as investors resumed a blue-chip buying spree after selling shares the day before to cash in profits.

The market's benchmark, the Nikkei average of 225 leading shares, rose 570.68 points or 3.19 percent to end the morning session at 18,434.72. On Thursday, the average had dropped sharply after a rally led by shares in export-oriented multinationals was snuffed out by a weaker dollar.
Comments by U.S. Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan overnight that there was too much pessimism over Japan's future provided the market with psychological support, they said.
The stock market has been hurt since the start of the year by concern over bad loans in the financial sector and the fragile basis of the nation's economic recovery.
"Bargain hunting for blue chips set in after the benchmark tumbled over two percent on Thursday," said Keiji Arai of Sanyo Securities.
"After the recent wild swings, the market is gradually reaching the consensus that a floor may exist at around the 17,300 level and that too was encouraging," Arai said.
The dollar's setback on Thursday in its recent headlong ascent had hurt stocks because a strong yen can curb the competitiveness of Japanese exports in overseas markets.
On the Tokyo foreign exchange market on Friday, the dollar was trading around the level of its New York close, standing at around 121.85 yen in early afternoon trade.
The comments in Washington by Greenspan sent stock traders scrambling to cover short positions, brokers said.
Greenspan, responding to a question during testimony before the Senate on Thursday, said: "Their (Japan's) history suggests that their pessimism at this stage is probably being grossly overdone."
However, despite the sharp gains, brokers said that selling pressure was heavy at a Nikkei level of 18,500 and it remained to be seen if the index can push above that.
In individual stocks, shares in Nippon Paper Industries Co Ltd rose 45 yen to 567 yen, buoyed by reports that two of its group firms had agreed to merge, brokers said.
Shares in Japan Paper Industry Co Ltd, one of the reported merger partners, were suspended for the whole day pending clarification of the reports. Company officials declined to comment.
Other Japanese share indices also rose, with TOPIX -- a more broadly based barometer than the blue-chip dominated Nikkei -- up 26.15 points, or 1.94 percent, at 1,371.85 by midsession.
